source.title: Continuous Diffusion Scales Competitively with Discrete Diffusion for Language
source.authors: Zhi-Han Yang; Wei Guo; Shui-Bai Zhang; Subham Sahoo; Yong-Xin Chen; Arash Vahdat; Morteza Mardani; John Thickstun

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study performs scaling sweeps of language-model validation loss over compute and model size, using an IsoFLOP analysis to estimate compute-optimal model sizes and losses. It applies this kind of measurement to continuous diffusion models and compares against autoregressive and discrete diffusion models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own scaling results and compute-optimal fits. The earlier 64× compute-gap result is cited background, not a result from this study. Other reported results, including downstream GSM8K accuracy and generation quality, do not test scale predictability.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own IsoFLOP sweep (6e18–1e20 non-embedding FLOPs, 14M–1.7B params, SlimPajama) for AR, MDLM, Duo and continuous-diffusion RePlaid. It fits compute-optimal validation loss and compute-optimal parameter count as power laws in compute. This is the Hoffmann IsoFLOP recipe applied to a new model family (diffusion LMs, with ELBO-bounded loss), so T3 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that, with architecture and protocol aligned, continuous diffusion (RePlaid) scales on par with discrete diffusion. Its compute gap to AR is ~20× (27× without self-conditioning) versus Plaid's earlier 64×. It uses fewer parameters at the compute-optimum and beats MDLM when over-trained. They flag that persistence at multi-billion scale is untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an IsoFLOP sweep and power-law fit for compute-optimal loss and model size, following a recent discrete-diffusion protocol. It evaluates continuous diffusion likelihood with variational upper bounds and counts non-embedding FLOPs; it does not reproduce the original Kaplan or Hoffmann training setup exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Self-conditioning changes the reported compute gap: ≈ 20× with it and ≈ 27× without it. The paper also states that its aligned architecture and experimental protocol differ from the setup behind the cited original Plaid compute-gap result.

fits_no_version.finding: Compute-optimal model size at a given budget differs by training objective. RePlaid (s.c.) uses ~3.4× fewer parameters than AR and ~1.8× fewer than MDLM/Duo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The compute-optimal parameter count depends on the generative training objective (AR vs diffusion variants), not only on compute.

fits_no_version.finding: In the over-trained regime RePlaid (s.c.) at ~3.1× its optimal compute matches MDLM at ~6.9× its optimal compute, so the methods' loss curves cross.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative standing of model families can flip between the compute-optimal and over-trained regimes.

record.problems: The authors state that error bars are absent for most experiments. The scaling sweep uses five compute budgets, and the paper notes that whether the trend persists in the multi-billion-parameter regime remains to be investigated. Diffusion losses are variational upper bounds, and fitted scaling coefficients are not reported.

untested.parts: Scaling over several orders of magnitude (compute spans only 6e18–1e20). Separate parameter-only and token-only laws. Fitted exponents are not reported.
No extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
Optimal token count vs compute. Exponent values, so no comparison of Kaplan vs Hoffmann allocation.
Depth/width vary across configurations (Tab. 10), but shape is not tested at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
GSM8K accuracy is reported at one 0.1B scale only.
No variation of fitting method, parameter counting, schedule or data to see exponent shifts.

missing.what: AR baseline's own compute-optimal loss vs compute power law (the reference curve for every compute gap)
Compute-optimal N* vs C fits for AR, MDLM, Duo and RePlaid (no s.c.)

record.verdict_notes: Diffusion LMs are still text language-model pretraining, so the results are filed under V1/V3 rather than V5. Losses for diffusion models are variational upper bounds, not exact NLL. There are only five compute budgets spanning ~1.2 orders of magnitude, there are no error bars, and no exponents are reported. The 64× Plaid figure is cited background. The MDLM 14× and Duo 22× gaps are reproductions of Sahoo et al. within this sweep.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests compute-optimal validation loss versus compute and reports IsoFLOP loss curves versus non-embedding parameter count. It does not test token-only scaling independently, report fitted exponents, or establish scaling for ordinary held-out NLL rather than the stated validation-loss measures (diffusion models use variational upper bounds).
No explicit test of whether fits from small runs predict the losses of runs orders of magnitude larger.
The study fits compute-optimal parameter count versus compute, but does not report an optimal-token-count versus compute fit or fitted exponents that compare parameter and token growth rates.
No controlled test of depth, width, or other architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
No tests of other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.
The paper reports a downstream task result at one model scale, but does not test whether downstream performance changes predictably with scale or pretraining loss.

The study does not systematically vary fitting method, parameter counting, schedule, or data to measure changes in fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation. Its comparison to the earlier 64× result is discussion of cited work, not a controlled rerun.

rows.subject: RePlaid (s.c.)

rows.operation_detail: IsoFLOP scaling sweep; fit compute-optimal validation loss against compute.

conditions.value: Validation loss; diffusion likelihood is a variational upper bound

rows.measure: Compute-optimal validation loss versus compute; reported compute gap to match AR validation loss.
rows.value: The compute-optimal loss exhibits power-law scaling, decreasing at a rate comparable to AR, MDLM, and Duo; RePlaid (s.c.) requires ≈ 20× the compute to match AR.
rows.note: The fitted power-law coefficients are not reported in the text.
rows.check: The value mixes the power-law statement with the 20× AR compute gap. Only the power-law part bears on V1. The compute range is only ~1.2 orders of magnitude, and the loss is an ELBO upper bound.

source_check.correct: For V1, state=cannot_determine. Section 3.3 fits a power law for perplexity, with log L equal to per-token NLL or its variational upper bound. This does not establish a power law for the pretraining loss itself. The approximately 20× AR compute gap is correctly reported.
source_check.problem: The reported perplexity power law does not establish V1's power law for held-out pretraining loss.

NeurIPS 2026 conference formatting is present; completed review is not established.
